implemented_requirements.requirement: Player controls snake using directional inputs
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py → _handle_keydown maps arrow/WASD keys to settings.UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT and calls snake.set_direction()

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake moves around the board each tick
implemented_requirements.evidence: snake.py → move() updates head position based on current direction and inserts it into body

implemented_requirements.requirement: Food items appear on random free cells
implemented_requirements.evidence: food.py → randomize_position() selects a random cell not in occupied set

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake grows when it eats food
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py → _step() checks new_head == food.get_position(), then calls snake.grow()

implemented_requirements.requirement: Score increases based on food eaten
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py → _step() adds SCORE_PER_FOOD * multiplier to self.score when food is eaten
game.py → _render() draws board, food, snake and HUD every frame
ui.py → draw_hud() renders the score, high score and difficulty
settings.py defines DIFFICULTIES; game.py provides a menu to select difficulty and adjusts move_interval and score multiplier

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete, classic Snake game: directional input, movement, food spawning, growth, collision detection, scoring, HUD, pause/menu, high‑score persistence, and selectable difficulty levels. The code appears syntactically correct and ready to run with pygame, so the benchmark requirements are satisfied.
